heroHeadline: Indian Intelligence Flags Possible Pakistani 'LoC Misadventure' Amid PoK Unrest; Ceasefire Holds at Day 489
heroSubtitle: September 11, 2026: Anonymous Indian Intelligence Bureau officials, in an IANS wire report published September 10, warned that Pakistan's military — under pressure from ongoing Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee-led strikes and sit-ins paralysing Rawalakot, Bhimber, Mirpur, Neelum Valley and Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, and from unrest in Balochistan — could attempt a diversionary 'misadventure' along the Line of Control, potentially a skirmish or an infiltration push, with Indian agencies described as on high alert. Separately on September 10, satellite-imagery reporting (unconfirmed by either government) described expanded Pakistani electronic-warfare infrastructure at Dadyal in PoK, roughly 33 km from the LoC, and at PAF Base Sindhri in Sindh. Neither report reflects a confirmed incident: no LoC firing, infiltration attempt or other cross-border event occurred September 10 or 11, and review of the preceding days found nothing new beyond Pakistan's September 8 reiteration of its rejection of India's UN 'Correct the Map' position on Jammu & Kashmir. The LoC has seen no firing or infiltration incidents since the August 27-29 drone cluster; the ceasefire holds at Day 489 with no confirmed cross-border fire exchange since May 10, 2025. Bilateral freeze remains otherwise comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT in abeyance.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
